name: Gilgal
overview: Gilgal is a significant location in Israel's history as the first encampment west of the Jordan River, marking the people's transition into the Promised Land (Joshua 4:19). It is the site where God commanded Joshua to renew the covenant of circumcision among the Israelites (Joshua 5:2), and where they celebrated the first Passover in Canaan (Joshua 5:10). At Gilgal, the miraculous provision of manna ceased as the Israelites began to eat the produce of the land (Joshua 5:11-12), symbolizing a new season of God's faithfulness. Additionally, Gilgal served as a center of leadership and covenant renewal, underscored by its role in key events such as the making of treaties (Joshua 9:6).
